To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a tetrameric purine has been synthesized by the successive Pd-catalysed cross-coupling reactions of two different dimeric units.
a tetrameric purine has been prepared by successive cross-coupling and subsequent Pd-catalysed cyclization, which is the only known synthesis of a quaterpurine.
a cyclic tetrameric purine (quartepurine) was synthesized in eight steps starting from 9‐benzyl‐6‐chloropurine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a new class of cyclic tetrameric purines, the so-called “quaterpurines”.
the synthesis of a cyclic tetrameric purine (quartpurine) 1.
the synthesis and characterization of a new type of quaterpurine, which is the first cyclic tetrameric purine with four N-6 and two N-8 substituents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of 2 is a very difficult task and the overall yield is low, although the synthesis is not very long and the number of synthetic operations is not high.
the synthesis of quaterpurines by the strategy presented herein, i.e. successive cross-couplings and subsequent cyclization, is not a practical approach to these compounds.
the Pd-cyclization of the tetrameric precursor 3b is the most efficient and reliable method to obtain the desired quaterpurine 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synthesis of a cyclic tetrameric purine is feasible by the successive formation of two C-6/C-C-8 bonds and subsequent Pd-catalysed intramolecular cross coupling reaction of a 6-iodo-8-chloro-quaterpurine.
we have succeeded to combine the four purine fragments 8a, 8a, and 8b to form the quaterpurine 2.
we have developed a new method to synthesize cyclic tetrameric purine derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to synthesize cyclic oligomers of nucleobases, which is a new class of nucleic acid analogues.
the Pd-coupling of two 8-iodopurene units is a very powerful tool in the construction of quaterpurines.
the tetrameric quaterpurine 2 can be obtained from the corresponding dimer 12 by a Pd-catalysed cross-coupling reaction.
